fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is not a defined escape from O19: fixed transport equations are linear, while assignment-dependent transports require a state expansion vulnerable to signed-flow splicing. No concrete graph, transport table, factor, target, or equal-completeness rule is supplied, so its proposed comparison is not yet executable.

Proposal 2 is blocked by O13/O15: any integral affine combination of honest enlarged codewords satisfies every linear Tanner check exactly. Expansion cannot give a nonzero syndrome to a codeword, and a bounded-degree Tanner graph has only O(N) local checks, contradicting the claimed Ω(N^{1+epsilon}) violations absent an accounted superlinear row family.

Proposal 3 merely renames the linear kernel as sheaf cohomology: affine pseudosections and signed cocycles remain zero-coboundary objects. Generic co-systolic expansion does not bound unrestricted integral coefficients for a formula-dependent sheaf, and no explicit complex or scaling theorem is supplied.

Proposal 4 fails because CVP digit and carry variables are unrestricted integers. Unless nonlinear digit membership is enforced, -1 has the constant-size representation d0=-1 with all higher digits zero; anchoring that coordinate costs O(1), not Ω(L), while linear carry restrictions remain exposed to O7/O15 affine lifting.

Proposal 5 is directly blocked by O15: the G13 affine combination of global assignment encodings lifts to every full bag and every projection with zero residual. Repeating bags multiplies both its anchor cost and the honest baseline, yielding no growing ratio.

Proposal 7 does not specify a primal CVP reduction: short dual evaluations and Nullstellensatz certificates do not themselves define a lattice factor and fixed target with the required distance orientation. Moreover, linear certificate degree gives exponentially many Macaulay monomials, so constant-degree tests cannot support the required polynomial-size general construction.
evidence: The supplied verifiers establish exact affine-span survival through compatible hashes and a laminar hierarchy (G13/G15), signed splicing in an emitted branching program (G19), and additive two-copy parity despite 125 cross-copy rows (G32). These are direct blockers for Proposals 1–5, not merely failed heuristics.

G31 shows that an equal-radius linear Gram can beat 4/3 on one finite instance, but G32 shows that block or moment-additive geometry does not compose. No proposal may convert either finite result into an asymptotic claim.

Proposal 6 is the only candidate with a potentially discriminating mutation: placing all exterior tags in one shared ambient block creates dense cross-clause Gram terms rather than independent Walsh energy. Exterior terminology alone adds no nonlinearity, so the experiment must determine whether equal-completeness forces a tight-frame collapse or whether the compatible two-parity witness becomes genuinely nonadditive.

O1/O6 require every tag, contraction, center, and normalization row to be emitted; O7/O9/O11/O12/O13/O19 require explicit evaluation of radix, parity, drop, affine, and signed-flow witnesses. O28/O30 remain untouched, and O32 requires a two-copy test before any continuation.
next_experiment: Preregister exact integral six-coordinate bivectors for all eight labels and a canonical incidence-sign rule independent of obstruction-shell outcomes; reject immediately unless all 16 globally consistent encodings have a certified common completeness bound and the rational Gram, factor, center, and matched control are fully emitted. Then exactly audit one and two copies against G7, G11/G13, DROP, G19, and compatible two-copy parity; continue only if the squared NO/completeness ratio strictly improves from one copy to two, otherwise kill Proposal 6.
